glosses: To include so that it no longer has separate existence; to overwhelm; to cause to disappear as if by swallowing up; to incorporate; to assimilate; to take in and use up.

examples.text: Dark oblivion soon absorbs them all.

In some countries, the large cities absorb the wealth and fashion of the nation; they are the only fixed abodes of elegant and intelligent society, and the country is inhabited almost entirely by boorish peasantry.

As a microbullet impacts the graphene, the diameter of the cone it creates – determined by later examination of the petals – provides a way to measure how much energy the graphene absorbs before breaking.
Wages absorbed 80% of the total revenue (which was inescapable), and they were rising at almost twice the rate of fares, which were pegged by law.

glosses: To engulf, as in water; to swallow up.

examples.text: to be absorpt, or swallowed up, in a lake of fire and brimstone.

glosses: To suck up; to drink in; to imbibe, like a sponge or as the lacteals of the body; to chemically take in.
To be absorbed, or sucked in; to sink in.

examples.text: The drops of water slowly absorbed into the dry sponge.

glosses: To take in energy and convert it.

examples.text: Heat, light, and electricity are absorbed in the substances into which they pass.

To engross or engage wholly; to occupy fully.

examples.text: Geeka was cooking dinner. As the little girl played she prattled continuously to her companion, propped in a sitting position with a couple of twigs. She was totally absorbed in the domestic duties of Geeka – so much so that she did not note the gentle swaying of the branches of the tree above her as they bent to the body of the creature that had entered them stealthily from the jungle.
Livonian affairs held him tight, and were to absorb him for many a year.

glosses: To occupy or consume time.
To assimilate mentally.

examples.text: If we fail to absorb the lessons of history, we are doomed to repeat them.

glosses: To assume or pay for as part of a commercial transaction.

examples.text: Among the most debatable is the contention that the profit margins of small employers are insufficient to absorb the costs of health insurance

glosses: To defray the costs.

examples.text: I’ll absorb the charge for the window replacement.

glosses: To accept or purchase in quantity.
To use up.

examples.text: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

glosses: To eat.

examples.text: Baby birds consume their own weight in food each day.

Concerns were raised around the ability of Milky Way species to consume proteins from Andromeda, so seed banks formed a significant part of the arks' cargo. We now know it is safe to consume food grown or hunted here, though enzyme supplements are recommended and have become a social norm at mealtimes.

glosses: To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.

examples.text: Desire consumed him.

glosses: To destroy completely.

examples.text: The building was consumed by fire.
If he were putting to my house the brand / That shall consume it.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through to steal: […]

glosses: To waste away slowly.

examples.text: Therefore, let Benedick, like cover'd fire, / Consume away in sighs.
But, sir, you see how weak I am. You must see that I have been consuming from day to day […].
He assured her the child was consuming at that moment in the next room.

glosses: To trade money for good or services as an individual.

examples.text: In a materialistic society, individuals are taught to consume, consume, consume.
If you consume this product while in Japan, you may be subject to consumption tax.

glosses: To absorb information, especially through the mass media.

examples.text: The Internet has changed the way we consume news.

glosses: To overwhelm.

examples.text: Depression engulfed her after her daughter's death.
Shaken by the biggest challenge to their authority in years, Brazil’s leaders made conciliatory gestures on Tuesday to try to defuse the protests engulfing the nation’s cities.

The blank spaces of Mallarmé, the silence of Maesterlinck, the inaniloquous repetitive babblings of Gertrude Stein are the abyss which threatens to engulf creative effort if it continues in this direction.

glosses: To surround; to cover; to submerge.

examples.text: Only Noah and his family survived when the Flood engulfed the world.
